class.name: VARaytracedSource
class.description: Base class for spatialised 3D sound sources that cast their own raytracing rays for reverb, ambience, and visualisation, regardless of how they get audio into OpenAL - see [VASource] (fixed [AudioStream] playback) and [VAStreamSource] (live pushed PCM playback). Muffling (occlusion/permeation) is applied to it by the listener's own rays, so this node never casts occlusion or permeation rays itself - use [VAEmitter]'s occlusion/permeation settings on the listener to control muffling.

method.name: is_raytraced
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once the world has completed at least one raytracing pass since this source joined it, so its reverb/ambience results are populated. This is [i]not[/i] the same as the listener having muffled this source - use [method is_raytraced_by_listener] for that.

method.name: is_raytraced_by_listener
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once the world's listener has actually raytraced this source, i.e. [method get_muffling_gain_lf] / [method get_muffling_gain_hf] reflect a real listener-to-source occlusion result rather than the unmuffled default. Stricter than [method is_raytraced].

method.name: get_muffling_gain_lf
method.description: How muffled this source currently is, as a low-frequency gain in the range [code]0..1[/code] ([code]1[/code] = not muffled at all). Returns [code]1.0[/code] until the listener has raytraced this source - guard with [method is_raytraced_by_listener].

method.name: get_muffling_gain_hf
method.description: How muffled this source currently is, as a high-frequency gain in the range [code]0..1[/code] ([code]1[/code] = not muffled at all). High frequencies drop first through obstacles, so [code]1.0 - get_muffling_gain_hf()[/code] is a good "how muffled" indicator. Returns [code]1.0[/code] until the listener has raytraced this source - guard with [method is_raytraced_by_listener].

members.member: Raytrace once on playback, then remove the emitter. Recommended for short sounds.
The number of reverb rays to cast.
The maximum number of bounces per reverb ray. Reverb rays stop bouncing after reaching the edge of the world when the world's "is indoors" setting is false.
The percentage of returning energy required for reverb to be at maximum volume.
The loudest volume that this source's sound will ever be played at.
How long, in milliseconds, the echogram records data for. Returning reverb rays after this period are ignored.
The length, in milliseconds, of each entry in the echogram.
If [code]true[/code], this source's EAX is blended into the grouped EAX returned by the world.
If [code]true[/code], this source's reverb send uses the listener's reverb effect rather than its own.
The percentage of occlusion energy required for this source to be at full volume.
The percentage of permeation energy required for this source to be at full volume.
The number of ambient occlusion rays to cast.
The maximum number of bounces per ambient occlusion ray. Ambient occlusion rays stop bouncing after reaching the edge of the world.
The percentage of ambient occlusion energy required for ambience to be at full volume.
The number of ambient permeation rays to cast.
The number of bounces per ambient permeation ray.
The percentage of ambient permeation energy required for ambience to be at full volume.
A user-defined integer tag for categorising sources.

The number of trails that are rebuilt from scratch each frame, to prevent staleness when this source moves. Trails are only rebuilt if the initial bounce position has strayed too far from the new bounce position.

The distance threshold for recreating trails, to prevent staleness when this source moves. Trails are only rebuilt once the initial bounce position has strayed further than this from the new bounce position.
The seed used to randomise scattering vectors. Randomised per source by default.
